entry.title: Does Gradient-Based Jailbreak Detection Hold Up in Multi-Turn Conversations?
entry.summary: Does the Unsafe Gradient Survive a Conversation? On the Fragility of Gradient-Based Jailbreak Detection in Multi-Turn Dialogue arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper examines whether GradSafe, a gradient-based jailbreak detector designed for single prompts, works in multi-turn dialogue. The authors add a Context Window Scanner that scores fixed-size windows of user turns and uses the highest window score for the whole conversation. Performance is strong on synthetic benign conversations (ROC-AUC 0.98) but drops to 0.76 on real WildChat conversations and varies with attack type and target model.

entry.title: pikit: A Toolkit for Testing Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
entry.summary: pikit: A Composable Toolkit for Indirect Prompt Injection Research and Evaluation arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents pikit, a research toolkit for systematically evaluating indirect prompt injection, where malicious instructions hidden in external content manipulate LLM agents. It covers 13 attack methods, 16 carriers across text and file modes, and 9 prevention strategies plus 3 offline detection baselines. In tests, the best prevention strategies reduced attack success rate by 71.8% relative, with few_shot_warning and instruction_hierarchy performing strongest. Offline detectors had perfect precision but low recall, suggesting they complement rather than replace prompt-level defenses.

entry.title: Survey of attacks that slow deep learning inference and how to defend against them
entry.summary: Deep Learning Latency Attacks and Defenses: A Cross-Domain Survey of Availability Threats arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This survey reviews adversarial attacks that aim to increase inference time, energy use, or response latency rather than change predictions. It covers perception pipelines, input-adaptive neural networks, and autoregressive and agentic systems such as LLMs and tool-using agents. The authors classify attacks by the computational bottleneck they exploit and propose a work-budget defense abstraction. The paper also analyzes when added model cost becomes a system-level availability failure, along with threat models, defenses, and open challenges.

entry.title: Efficient library-boundary compartmentalization on CHERI hardware
entry.summary: Efficient Linkage-Based Compartmentalization on CHERI arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents a linkage-based model for in-process compartmentalization using CHERI memory safety, applied across the entire UNIX user space. It scales to over 10,000 compartments on desktop systems and creates 500+ compartments per process for large applications such as Chromium. Of thousands of C/C++ programs tested, only the V8 engine needed source changes. The model is implemented for CHERI-extended Armv8-A and RISC-V. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present a linkage-based in-process compartmentalization model on CHERI that splits along existing library boundaries, reporting 500+ compartments per process for Chromium and evaluating on

entry.title: Understanding Private Evolution as a learning-augmented clustering method for private synthetic data
entry.summary: Understanding Private Evolution as Learning-Augmented Clustering arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Private Evolution is a differentially private method for generating synthetic data. This paper recasts it as Wasserstein learning augmented by a generative model, and shows theoretically that better performance bounds are possible when the generator captures some features of the true distribution. The authors find that standard PE variants can fail to converge on simple well-clustered instances, and they propose a geometry-aware version that provably converges on such instances. Experiments show the new algorithm is competitive with standard baselines and can improve recall.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Defense: Continual Security Policy Learning for LLM Agents
entry.summary: Self-Evolving Defense: Continual Security Policy Learning for LLM Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper introduces Self-Evolving Defense (SED), a training-free framework that turns harmful agent trajectories into reusable security policies without updating model weights. It retrieves relevant policies for new tasks to adapt to emerging attacks while retaining knowledge across attack types. Tested on three open-source models and eight benchmarks covering jailbreaks, prompt injection, and insecure code generation, SED reportedly lowers AGENTDOJO prompt-injection success to 0.42% and adaptive X-TEAMING attack success on HARMBENCH to 7.8%, while preserving benign task utility.

entry.title: CyberPersistBench: Testing whether AI attack agents can keep access after a break-in
entry.summary: CyberPersistBench: Evaluating LLM-Based Cyber Attackers on Installation and Persistence arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper introduces CyberPersistBench, the first benchmark for evaluating whether LLM-based attackers can install and maintain access after initial compromise. Agents must keep footholds across staged system disruptions using native host mechanisms, scored on a six-level deterministic scale (L1–L6) over 203 core tasks. Across five frontier agents, autonomous persistence reached only 27.6%–44.8%, falling to 5.5%–13.3% on defense-enabled tasks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce the first benchmark for post-compromise installation and persistence, using deterministic six-level scoring across 203 core tasks and defense extensions. They report autonomous p

entry.title: CounterSteer: Blocking Hidden Instructions in AI Agent Tool Results
entry.summary: CounterSteer: Suppressing Indirect Prompt Injection with Activation Steering arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Indirect prompt injection makes language model agents follow instructions hidden in untrusted retrieved text. CounterSteer is an inference-time defense that fits a direction inside the model from paired examples and subtracts it from tool-result tokens during prefill. Across five open-weights models, held-out attack success and AgentDojo compromise rates drop sharply while benign utility stays high. Attacker-chosen parameters inside legitimate calls are only partially resisted. ★★★★★ Notable: Applies inference-time activation steering to tool-result tokens to suppress indirect prompt injection; the authors report lower attack success across five open-weights models and adaptive attacks whi

entry.title: ANCHOR: Context-grounded, stateful LLM investigation of system provenance for attack tracing
entry.summary: Know the Normal, Track the Attack: Context-Grounded and Stateful LLM Investigation over System Provenance arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents ANCHOR, a system that turns suspicious activity flagged by provenance-based intrusion detection into coherent attack narratives. It combines curated evidence with context-grounded LLM reasoning, using deployment-specific normal-behavior baselines and a confidence-gated cache that tracks attack state across time windows. The authors evaluate it on six DARPA Transparent Computing E3/E5 datasets and report better IoC recovery and attack-stage attribution than existing provenance-based baselines.

entry.title: FinRT: Reusable Adversarial Prompt Generators for Testing Consumer Finance AI
entry.summary: FinRT: Distilling Adaptive Red-Teaming Strategies into Reusable Adversarial Generators in Consumer Finance arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents FinRT, a framework that distills adaptive red-teaming strategies into reusable adversarial prompt generators for consumer finance, where harmless-looking queries can cause large language models to fail safety checks. Across six victim models, FinRT nearly doubles the attack success rate of the adaptive baseline Rainbow Teaming (32.9% vs. 17.2%) and increases maximum adversarial severity by 33%. It keeps semantic diversity within policy domains comparable to iterative search methods and shows high cross-model transferability.

entry.title: Quantization makes private dense retrieval practical against malicious servers
entry.summary: Quantization Enables Private Dense Retrieval against Malicious Service Providers arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Dense retrieval, a core part of retrieval-augmented generation, finds relevant documents by comparing vector representations of queries and passages. The paper formalizes private dense retrieval as protecting query privacy and retrieval integrity against a malicious server, and proposes a two-round cryptographic protocol that uses low-bit quantization to keep computation practical. Across six embedding models and corpora up to 2.68 million passages, three-bit quantization with a clipped quantizer largely preserves retrieval quality and downstream RAG accuracy. A private query over a clinical-reference-sized corpus takes one to three minutes of server time.

entry.title: Audience-bound persistent memory: authorization across the whole memory lifecycle
entry.summary: Audience-Bound Persistent Memory: Authorization Across the Memory Lifecycle arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how a personal language agent acting for its owner across private and shared conversations should authorize memory before assembling context. Each memory item records the audience present when it was made, and a memory enters a model's context only if every current viewer belongs to an authorized audience. The approach was implemented in two independent architectures and an agent-memory runtime. In a pre-registered test over 10,000 multi-party histories, no forbidden item entered any architecture's context, while unscoped retrieval exposed forbidden items in 82% of contexts. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes audience-bound memory admission across the lifecycle; over 10,000 multi-party histories, no forbidden item entered context while unscoped retrieval exposed them in 82%.

entry.title: TTMark: Pairwise Watermarking That Makes AI Text Easier to Detect
entry.summary: TTMark: Pairwise Distortion-Free Watermarking Beyond Single-Token Entropy arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents TTMark, a watermarking framework that extends distortion-free watermarking from single tokens to adjacent token pairs. By watermarking the joint distribution of consecutive tokens, the detector can use both token entropy and conditional entropy. Experiments across several language models and datasets report better detectability without degrading generation quality.

entry.title: Conversable quantum fire in the standard model: quantum states that clone easily but cannot be sent by one-way classical messages
entry.summary: Conversable Quantum Fire in the Standard Model arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper presents a construction of quantum fire, quantum states that can be efficiently cloned but cannot be transmitted by one-way classical communication. Unlike earlier provably untelegraphable constructions, which rely on an oracle, this one is based on one-shot signatures and works in the standard model. The authors introduce keyless untelegraphability and conversability, meaning fire can be transferred via two-way classical interaction. Two variants are given, supporting polynomially and exponentially many flames respectively.

entry.title: Calibrating Membership Inference Attacks Using Neighboring Samples
entry.summary: Calibrating One-Round Membership Inference with Neighbors arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Membership inference attacks test whether a given example was part of a model's training data. The strongest current methods need reference models trained for each example, which is too costly for large models. This paper asks whether neighboring samples of the target can provide the calibration needed when only one trained model is available, without training extra models. The authors propose two ways to obtain such neighbors and show that querying an early training checkpoint sharpens the signal. Experiments on three image classification datasets and three training setups report strong membership signals and competitive attack performance at no additional training cost.

entry.title: DecoyTrace: Using Toxic Decoys to Actively Defend Decentralized Federated Learning
entry.summary: DecoyTrace: Toxic Decoys for Active Defense in Decentralized Federated Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper addresses decentralized federated learning, where there is no central server and malicious updates such as backdoors can evade passive parameter checks. It proposes DecoyTrace, which deploys a mobile decoy node that sends decoy challenges and dual clean and decoy models based on neighbor trust, then evaluates them with three-state semantic metrics. Once an attack is confirmed, a distributed protocol isolates the source and resets or recovers the model. Across 60 configurations on the NEBULA platform, the F1-score stays within 0.03 of the baseline on MNIST and FashionMNIST and is 0.05 to 0.10 lower on CIFAR-10, while CPU and network usage drop by up to two-thirds.

entry.title: Empirical Study of EU AI Act Compliance Checker Tools
entry.summary: An Empirical Study and Assessment of EU AI Act Compliance Checkers arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents the first empirical study of automated tools that check compliance with the EU AI Act. The authors characterize 12 mainstream checkers, evaluate their legal coverage and alignment, and analyze the structure, determinacy, and actionability of their generated reports. They find that checker quality varies significantly, that the tools can serve only as early-stage orientation, and that they tend to oversimplify or omit key obligations. The paper also offers design principles for more reliable compliance-support tools.

entry.title: Adversarial debiasing of machine learning models to improve DDoS attack detection for network security
entry.summary: Adversarial Debiasing of Machine Learning Models for Enhanced Network Security against DDoS Attacks arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper proposes a DDoS detection method that uses GAN-generated synthetic traffic data to train a Random Forest classifier. Adversarial debiasing is applied to reduce sensitivity to skewed packet-related features. The authors report 99.98 percent accuracy on benchmark data and a 22.60 percent improvement on previously unseen synthetic traffic.

entry.title: Privacy-friendly audience grouping: on-device, in-browser job-segment inference for ID-free ads
entry.summary: Privacy-Friendly Cohort Determination: Sealed, CSP-Independent In-Browser ML Inference of Professional Segments for Identity-Less Advertising arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents SIF (Sealed Inference Frame), which infers coarse professional cohorts on the user's device inside the browser and sends only a locally differentially private, taxonomy-coded label into the OpenRTB bid stream, with no cross-site identifier. It reports privacy-utility trade-offs, a re-identification simulation, and an assessment of which attributes are predictable. The authors find that company type and size are predictable, while seniority largely is not.

entry.title: Rendering Inputs as Images to Defend Against Prompt Injection
entry.summary: Render Before Reading: Visual Rendering as a Prompt Injection Defense arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper finds that multimodal LLMs are more likely to follow adversarial instructions delivered as text than when the same instructions arrive as images. Building on this modality gap, the authors propose Pictionary, a training-free defense that renders untrusted content as typographic images or audio before it reaches the model. Across ten models and two benchmarks, the method consistently reduces attack success rates while largely preserving benign utility, including against adaptive attacks and human red teamers. ★★★★★ Notable: Finds multimodal LLMs follow text-form injected instructions more than image-form ones, and proposes a training-free rendering defense that the authors report reduces attack success across ten models

entry.title: Multi-Class, Multi-Tier Network Intrusion Detection: A Reproducible Benchmark
entry.summary: Multi-Class, Multi-Tier Network Intrusion Detection: A Comprehensive and Reproducible Benchmark arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper addresses inconsistent and inflated results on the CIC-IDS2017 intrusion detection dataset by correcting PCAP-level labels and building a complete evaluation pipeline. Eleven tabular classifiers are assessed at three levels: binary attack detection, nine-class attack-family attribution, and fifteen-class fine-grained classification. A soft-voting ensemble of Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM achieves the best fine-tier macro-F1 of 0.955. The configurable pipeline is released as open source.

entry.title: When Privacy Becomes a Weapon: Doxxing and Privacy Risks on Mainland China's Social Media
entry.summary: When Privacy Becomes a Weapon: Understanding Doxxing and Privacy Vulnerabilities in Mainland China's Social Media Ecosystem arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies doxxing, the malicious disclosure of personal information, in mainland China. Through semi-structured interviews with 18 survivors, the authors build a framework describing how doxxing operates in this setting. They find that platform amplification resembles Western patterns, while compulsory identity linkage, nationalist discourse, fandom culture, Confucian values and low privacy literacy create China-specific dynamics. The authors argue that protection requires constraining systemic vulnerabilities and propose recommendations for legal reform, platform design and social initiatives.

entry.title: PrivacySkills: How Privacy Guidance Shapes Which Information Sources LLM Agents Pick
entry.summary: PrivacySkills: How Privacy Guidance Shapes Source Selection in LLM Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper introduces PrivacySkills, a controlled framework for testing how LLM agents choose among ways to obtain the same task information, such as public personal data, confidential sources, or asking the user. It uses 55 synthetic tasks and 169 skills, comparing system-level instructions with skill-level privacy labels. Without privacy guidance, agents accessed confidential sources in 30% of valid runs, rising to 45% when users were unavailable, while urgency framing had no detectable effect. Combining system instructions with skill-level labels roughly halved confidential access.

entry.title: Same Text, Different Authority: How Reserved Tokens Make Chat-Template Prompt Injection Stronger
entry.summary: Same Bytes, Different Authority: Reserved-Token Representations in Chat-Template Prompt Injection arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies prompt injection against LLM agents, finding that forged chat-template markers such as <|im_start|> are far more effective when fed to the model as reserved control tokens than as ordinary subwords. Encoding the same text as subwords lowered attack success on the InjecAgent benchmark by 39 to 66 percentage points on three of four open-weight families. The standard tokenizer mitigation covers only tokens a configuration declares special, so tool-protocol tokens remain unprotected and the gap persists on that channel. ★★★★★ Notable: Shows that the same text encoded as a reserved control token versus subwords changes forged-marker injection authority, quantified on InjecAgent and AgentDojo, with implications for defense.

entry.title: TEE Anchor: Cross-TEE organizational endorsement to reduce physical attacks on TEEs
entry.summary: TEE Anchor: Cross-TEE Organizational Endorsement for Mitigating TEE Physical Attacks arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 In 2025, practical physical-access attacks on TEEs, such as TEE.fail and Battering RAM, were disclosed. The paper proposes TEE Anchor, a lightweight X.509-based mechanism in which an organization issues certificates over each CPU's Chip ID to form its own PKI, and a Verifier checks the Chip ID in attestation evidence to prove the machine's organizational affiliation. It needs no extra root of trust such as a (v)TPM, and the prototype's operations, including provisioning and verification, complete within a few milliseconds.

entry.title: MMSkillRisk: Can AI agents stay safe when image-based skills hide malicious instructions?
entry.summary: MMSkillRisk: Can Agents Stay Safe When Multimodal Skills Become Traps? arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces MMSkillRisk, a benchmark for end-to-end safety testing of attacks hidden in images within multimodal agent skills. The authors design NCVA, an attack that disguises malicious instructions as native parts of teaching images, such as annotations and interface labels. Across nine model-harness configurations, NCVA reaches a pooled attack success rate of 43.1%, 16.4 percentage points above a text-carrier baseline. The results show attacks can succeed while legitimate tasks are also completed, so task success alone does not prove safe skill use. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report that NCVA, an image-borne attack, reaches 43.1% pooled ASR in isolated sandboxes, 16.4 points above the text-carrier baseline across nine configurations.

entry.title: Similarity Is Not Validity: Defending LLM Semantic Caches Against Poisoning
entry.summary: Similarity Is Not Validity: Defending LLM Semantic Caches Against Poisoning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Semantic caches cut LLM serving costs by reusing answers to similar queries, but retrieval relies only on embedding similarity, so an attacker can store a malicious answer under a query that looks benign. The paper proposes a defense that recovers distinguishing information from the raw cache-key text, exploiting a rewrite-residual structure in adversarial queries. Using Deletion Gain and an Answer Check, it blocks 82.0% to 98.2% of poisoned entries across three attack classes at a 5% false-positive rate, with negligible serving overhead.

entry.title: Raising the Bar for Chinese Adolescent LLM Safety: A Culturally-Grounded Benchmark
entry.summary: Raising the Bar for Chinese Adolescent LLM Safety: A Culturally-Grounded, Fine-Grained Benchmark arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper introduces QH-Bench, a Chinese-language benchmark for adolescent content safety, built on Chinese social and cultural scenarios, with 715 single-turn items and 100 four-turn trajectories. Evaluating 13 open-weight models, it finds offline-contact scenarios to be a shared weakness, with every model scoring negatively on over half of such items. The authors note that leading aggregate scores do not show these specific weaknesses have been resolved.

entry.title: SaplingGuard: A Profile-Aware Multi-Agent Safety Guardrail for Adolescent-LLM Chats
entry.summary: SaplingGuard: A Multidimensional-Profile-Aware Multi-Agent Guardrail for Developmentally Safe Adolescent-LLM Interaction arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper introduces SaplingGuard, a plug-and-play safety guardrail that uses user profiles and dialogue context to detect implicit developmental risks when adolescents interact with LLMs, without modifying the downstream models. It uses three agents for profile construction, context-aware risk assessment, and intent-preserving prompt optimization. On SaplingBench, a set of 276 three-turn dialogues across seven developmental risk categories, the authors report that profile-aware retrieval raised the Major Hit rate and that the full intervention lowered the average harmful response rate.

entry.title: Taming Multi-Category Harms: Adaptive Safety Steering for LLMs
entry.summary: How to Tame a Multi-Headed Hydra? Adaptive Multi-Category Safety Steering for Large Language Models arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper proposes CAM-Steer, a framework that improves LLM safety by modifying internal activations during inference without updating model parameters. It estimates the risk of each harm category by comparing the hidden state with safe and unsafe prototypes, then combines category-specific safety directions into one steering direction and sets the intervention strength. Experiments across three LLM backbones and seven harm categories show higher average defense success rates than the evaluated baselines, including when categories co-occur, with negligible inference overhead.

entry.title: Climbing the Hill: Curriculum RL Red-Teaming for Prompt Injection Against Frontier Models
entry.summary: Climbing the Hill: Prompt Injection Red-Teaming Against Frontier Models with Curriculum Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper studies prompt injection, a major security risk for LLMs and LLM-based agents, and proposes a curriculum reinforcement learning method for red-teaming. It addresses the cold-start problem, where an attacker model receives no learning signal because every attack fails against frontier models. The attacker is trained against progressively more robust targets, with each stage partially succeeding to provide learning signals. On AgentDyn, the reported attack success rates (ASR@10) are 93.8% against GPT-5.6-Luna and 45.0% against GPT-5.6-Terra, while RL-Hammer and PISmith achieve 0%.

entry.title: Distillation defenses can fail after reinforcement learning
entry.summary: Distillation Defenses Easily Break After Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies distillation attacks that copy the reasoning abilities of closed-source language models, and the defenses against them. The authors argue that existing defenses are usually tested only right after distillation, ignoring further training with reinforcement learning. They show that simple attacks using data easily available from current APIs can match the reasoning gains of attacks that extract full hidden traces. They conclude that defenses leaking enough information to reconstruct approximate reasoning traces are likely ineffective.

entry.title: Short proofs for quantum problems using only basic hash-function assumptions
entry.summary: Succinct Arguments for QMA from Collapsing Hash Functions arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper shows that succinct arguments for QMA exist assuming only collapsing hash functions. This is the first such scheme relying only on unstructured Minicrypt assumptions, not known to imply public-key encryption. A key component is a quantum-succinct claw-state generation protocol that uses classical communication to expand a few quantum correlations into many claw-state correlations. Combined with a communication-compression compiler, this yields succinct arguments for QMA with better round complexity and a simpler standard-model proof than prior work. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first QMA succinct arguments assuming only collapsing hash functions, relying solely on unstructured Minicrypt assumptions. Their claw-state generation protocol uses only classi

entry.title: AI Virus Spreading via Shared Files Between LLM Agents
entry.summary: Share-Borne AI Virus: Memory-Hopping Attacks Across LLM Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how large language model assistants that share persistent artifacts, such as reports, can unintentionally pass adversarial content between one another. Malicious content is stored in an assistant's memory, reproduced in later artifacts, and picked up by other assistants. The authors simulate artifact exchange among independent assistants to measure survival across hand-offs, hop count, and spread. They report that attacks propagate across multiple assistants and reach 60-80% of agents in larger simulations, with chains extending to eight hops. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a self-propagating attack spreading via shared artifacts across independent assistants, reporting 60-80% agent reach and eight-hop chains in larger simulations.

entry.title: INTCC: A framework enabling interactive work inside confidential computing environments
entry.summary: INTCC: A Framework for Interactive Confidential Computing arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper proposes interactive confidential computing, a model that lets untrusted data processors run dynamic, human-guided operations inside Trusted Execution Environments while keeping data confidential. The authors split the TEE into an interactive controller and a verifiable runtime, and implement the INTCC framework on AMD SEV-SNP using Confidential Containers. Reported experiments show overhead below 5% for LLM fine-tuning and under 17% for data analysis compared with baseline execution.

entry.title: Detecting Fake Data Attacks and Unstable Operation in Smart Grids Using Graph Learning
entry.summary: Detecting False Data Injection and Unstable Operation in Smart Grid via System-Aware Graph Boundary Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper introduces StarGNN, a graph learning framework that learns the stable operating region only from clean stable configurations. It uses a single abnormality score to flag reported configurations that should not be trusted, covering both real instability and false data injection attacks. Each configuration is modeled as a producer-consumer star graph, and physics-constrained pseudo-negatives are generated by perturbing reaction time and price response parameters. On nine unseen attack scenarios, the method detects 0.780 to 0.973 of attacks on stable configurations and keeps post-attack instability recall between 0.972 and 0.999.

entry.title: Beyond Scalar Probes: Using Vector Outputs of ReLU Networks to Extract Signatures
entry.summary: Beyond Scalar Probes: Exploiting Vector-Valued Outputs in ReLU Networks For Signature Extraction arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper revisits cryptanalytic extraction of ReLU networks from a geometric and algebraic perspective. Instead of examining a single output component, it studies the full vector-valued behavior across adjacent linear regions and characterizes Jacobian differences as rank-one, recovering row-signature information along with complementary column-side information. Experiments show this extra structure can aid extraction and improve numerical estimation under float64, float32, and float16 precision. The analysis is extended from high-precision, output-rounding settings to low-precision settings common in practice.

entry.title: Using LLMs to Automatically Prove Security of Cryptographic Protocols: Current Capabilities
entry.summary: LLM-Assisted Automatic Security Proofs for Cryptographic Protocols: How Far Are We? arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper systematically evaluates how well state-of-the-art large language models assist in verifying cryptographic symbolic protocols. It introduces CRoST (Coverage Rate of Solve Tree), a proof-based metric that measures how similar generated lemmas are to reference lemmas. Models achieve 38.82% coverage on average, and 14.4% of generated lemmas exceed 80% coverage. However, the models show failures on complex multi-phase protocols, diminishing returns from naive scaling, and substantial verification overhead.

entry.title: Indistinguishability of permutation sums via Fourier analysis for classical and quantum security
entry.summary: Indistinguishability of Sum of Permutations: A Fourier Analytic Route to Classical and Quantum Security arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies whether sums of independent random permutations, and related constructions, can be told apart from random functions under classical and quantum query models. It uses a unified Fourier analytic approach to derive query-dependent security bounds in both models. The authors also analyse linear postprocessing over binary vector spaces and Dinur's variable-output single-permutation construction.

entry.title: AI-Based Vulnerability Assessment and Cyber Attack Graph Analysis
entry.summary: AI-Based Vulnerability Assessment Capability and Cyber Attack Graph Analysis arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper combines two methods for assessing cyber risk to critical infrastructure. One uses multi-agent reinforcement learning over a cyber knowledge graph to identify attack vectors and TTPs; the other is a probabilistic attack graph model that computes system-level risk from network topology and vulnerabilities. Applied independently to the same operational technology network and validated against the 2015 Ukraine power grid attack, both methods matched the documented attack vectors. The authors find industrial control systems to be the most critical enablers of attack propagation, making them priority targets for hardening.

entry.title: "Nothing to See Here": Accidental Leaks via LLM Revision Traces
entry.summary: "Nothing to See Here'': Unintended Disclosure through Revision Traces of LLM Deliverables arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how LLM assistants can unintentionally reveal information they were asked to remove, by restating the deleted item when describing the edit. An analysis of public conversation corpora found revision traces in 8.8% of revision requests. Using the new RevLeakBench benchmark, the authors found that about half of deliverables state the edit, and a reader seeing only the deliverable could recover the withdrawn item in about 13% of them. The paper also compares prompt defenses and proposes an output-side filter that sharply reduces recovery.

entry.title: Planarian: Managing Agent State with Statepoints
entry.summary: Planarian: Managing Agent State with Statepoints arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents Planarian, an agent runtime that manages state using restorable point-in-time versions of the environment called statepoints. It offers snapshot, rollback, and fork primitives so agents and users can undo erroneous actions and explore alternatives in parallel across local and remote state. Remote state changes are reverted through recorded compensating actions. The authors report task quality improvements of up to 15x and only 3% overhead for users recovering from errors.

entry.title: Emulating Hybrid QKD and Post-Quantum Networks Automatically in the Cloud
entry.summary: Hybrid QKD-PQC Network Emulation through Automated and Scalable Cloud-Native Orchestration arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper extends Quditto, an open-source emulator originally built for quantum key distribution (QKD) networks, to support hybrid networks that combine QKD with post-quantum cryptography (PQC). The platform adds a cloud-native orchestrator, an optimized provisioning workflow for large deployments, native post-quantum nodes, and a secure key management module. Experiments on a representative spine-leaf deployment show that orchestration time scales sublinearly with network size and that end-to-end hybrid key establishment succeeds.

entry.title: Zero-knowledge proofs for quantum networks, a verification method that reveals no extra information
entry.summary: Zero Knowledge Proofs in Quantum Networks arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper develops a framework for zero-knowledge verification based on the indistinguishability of quantum states under operational constraints. It shows that, due to limits on local operations, a verifier cannot extract information about the underlying state yet can still check its correctness. The authors build explicit protocols for multiparty quantum networks that achieve information-theoretic security, meaning collaborating parties learn nothing beyond the statement's validity.

entry.title: Sustained Participation as a Security Resource: BPC
entry.summary: Sustained Participation as a Security Resource: The Bounded Participation Channel arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces the Bounded Participation Channel (BPC), a formal primitive that repeatedly verifies each identity's participation window by window using fresh, identity-bound challenges under strict deadlines. It proves a cost theorem: sustaining s identities over T windows requires at least sT/τ_h participation channel-windows. Tested AI systems reached 97–100% accuracy on perceptual tasks, yet their throughput remained bounded under the tested conditions.

entry.title: Continuous assurance for AI security auditors gating software releases
entry.summary: Continuous Assurance of Agentic Security Auditors for Software Delivery Decision Gates arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper addresses LLM-based repository auditors used as security controls in CI pipelines, whose findings decide whether code changes merge. It proposes the Policy-Evidence-Execution Separation Pattern, implemented as the TAIP Assurance Engine and operated as Continuous Control Posture Assurance, which binds admitted evidence to a versioned Posture Tree. The approach was evaluated with unmodified RepoAudit on a fixed Python null pointer dereference benchmark, using 80 executions across two OpenAI model configurations. On a single host, full policy-triggered recomputation across 1,000 independent assurance contexts took at most 1.62 s, below the predeclared 5 s budget.

entry.title: Building Data Diodes from Commodity Hardware and Open Source Software
entry.summary: Implementing Data Diodes Using Commodity Hardware and Open Source Software arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Data diodes are one-way network devices used to defend against sophisticated cyberattacks, mostly deployed in nuclear plants and government agencies. The paper shows that a data diode's hardware can be assembled from commodity fiber-optic equipment, and focuses on software needed to minimize packet loss, since the receiver cannot request retransmission. The authors found most loss came from slow receiver processing and often occurs in clusters, and identified reliable configurations for UDPcast and lidi among three tested open source programs. The findings were incorporated into pydiode, a cross-platform program for reliable one-way data transfers.

entry.title: Poster: Towards ProofWeave, a privacy-minimised, integrity-anchored evidence plane for continuous agentic AI assurance
entry.summary: Poster: Towards ProofWeave: A Privacy-Minimised, Integrity-Anchored Evidence Plane for Continuous Agentic Assurance arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper introduces ProofWeave, a record-time chain-of-evidence concept for agentic AI systems. At each policy-relevant action boundary it produces a privacy-minimised, integrity-anchored evidence transaction binding the agent's intent, the control response, and a policy-at-time snapshot, committed to an append-only ledger. In a scenario where an agent tries to send a secret to an unapproved external sink, it reduces candidate bindings per verdict, validation operations, and evidence storage compared with a logs-only correlation baseline.

entry.title: TANGO: Watermarking Text From Masked Diffusion Models Using Token Pairs
entry.summary: TANGO: Watermarking Masked Diffusion Language Models in Token Pairs arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents TANGO, a watermarking method for masked-diffusion language models that generate text by filling masked positions in parallel. Each new token is tied to a nearby already-unmasked token, with a secret key assigning vocabulary tokens to color classes and biasing the new token toward a color set by the key and that neighbor. Detection requires only the text and the key and does not assume any unmasking order. On two masked-diffusion models, TANGO detects nearly all unedited watermarked texts and most edited ones, and frequency attacks that forge a fixed green list fail against it.

entry.title: OT-PCA: A New Side-Channel Key-Recovery Attack on HQC Using Offline Templates and Plaintext-Checking Oracles
entry.summary: OT-PCA: New Key-Recovery Plaintext-Checking Oracle Based Side-Channel Attacks on HQC with Offline Templates arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents OT-PCA, a side-channel attack on the HQC post-quantum cryptosystem that uses a plaintext-checking oracle. It builds offline templates by calling the public HQC decoder and optimizes them with genetic-style algorithms. Simulations show fewer oracle calls than prior methods, including a 2.4-fold reduction for hqc-128, and robustness when oracle accuracy drops to 95%. A power analysis evaluation on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller validates the approach in practice.

entry.title: Tracking Security Debt Across LLM Coding Agent Trajectories
entry.summary: Trajectory-Level Security Debt in LLM Coding Agents arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies how security findings change over the many intermediate code states an LLM coding agent produces, arguing that evaluating only the final output misses this evolution. The authors propose the Security Debt Line Integral (SDLI), which accumulates static-analysis risk whenever an agent reaches a new best test pass ratio. Using four static application security testing tools on SWE-bench, ProgramBench, and MirrorCode runs, they report scanner-based findings rather than validated vulnerability rates.

entry.title: When Valid Tool Calls Change Meaning: Formation-Consistent Dispatch for LLM Agents
entry.summary: When Valid Tool Calls Change Meaning: Formation-Consistent Dispatch for LLM Agents arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper shows that agents form tool calls from model-visible interfaces, but hosts select the implementation later, so standard dispatch ignores the link between descriptor and handler. An unchanged, schema-valid call can therefore carry different security effects during rollout, reconnection, or delayed approval, which the authors call schema-epoch drift. They propose formation-consistent dispatch (FCD), which ties implementation analysis to execution authority and verifies each call's effects against its security contract. Across 32 official releases, 29 needed no release-specific change and three were escalated.

entry.title: Efficient TCitH-Based Alternatives to SLH-DSA: A Cross-Layer ASIC Design of Mirath
entry.summary: Efficient TCitH-Based Alternatives to SLH-DSA: Cross-Layer ASIC Design of Mirath arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 NIST has standardized several post-quantum signature schemes and is evaluating non-lattice alternatives to SLH-DSA. This paper presents the first ASIC implementation of Mirath, a TCitH-based signature scheme, in a RISC-V system using a cross-layer approach spanning algorithm and hardware. Implemented in 22nm FD-SOI technology, the design achieves 17.8x lower signing latency and 58% less total cell area than an SLH-DSA ASIC in the same technology node.

entry.title: Still There, No Longer Seen: Compression-Induced Risk in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: Still There, No Longer Seen: Exposing Compression-Induced Risk in Large Vision-Language Models arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies the risks that arise when Large Vision-Language Models compress visual tokens to reduce inference cost. The authors define a compression-specific failure as an adversarial input that is answered correctly with full tokens but fails after compression. They propose CIRA, an attack that perturbs images using only vision-encoder access to induce such failures. The paper also reports that a cross-view selection-stabilization defense substantially suppresses CIRA, though an adaptive variant partially restores its effectiveness.

entry.title: Cyclotomic Cosets: A Hidden-Subgroup Generalization and Quantum Sieve for LWE-Related Problems
entry.summary: Cyclotomic Cosets: Hidden Subgroup and Quantum Sieving Algorithm for Prime-Power Moduli arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces the Cyclotomic Coset Problem (CCP), a cyclotomic generalization of the Dihedral Coset Problem that keeps an exact hidden-subgroup structure. The authors build a quantum sieve using a π-adic ideal chain, which for fixed prime p and modulus q=p^t solves CCP in time and sample complexity 2^{O_p(log n log q)} with polynomial quantum space. The method also extends to uniform EDCP and Gaussian S|LWE>, but the authors state it does not by itself give a quasi-polynomial algorithm for standard LWE.

entry.title: Change Web State Before Acting: Protecting Web Agents from Deceptive Interfaces
entry.summary: Before Acting, Change the State: Prospective State Intervention for Web Agents under Deceptive Interfaces arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 LLM-based Web agents can complete user tasks autonomously, but deceptive interfaces can steer them toward outcomes against users' interests. The paper identifies a failure mode in which a task-valid action still causes an unauthorized consequence due to the current Web state. The proposed Veer defense builds a prospective intervention trajectory toward a safe state and verifies it before modifying the live environment. On TrickyArena and WebDecept, Veer achieves the highest safe task completion across three evaluation settings and reduces dark-pattern success on WebDecept to 0.3%.

entry.title: JevVibe: Classification-guided method for making AI-generated code more secure
entry.summary: JevVibe: Efficient Classification-Guided Secure Code Generation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper addresses security weaknesses in code generated by large language models. It introduces Jev, a decision model that selects Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) labels directly from candidates and returns probabilities, and evaluates it on a 50-way classification task using 1,916 CyberSecEval examples. Jev outperforms six open-weight baselines and, compared with GPT-5.6-Sol, performs better on Top-3 and Top-5 accuracy with much lower latency and cost. The authors also build JevVibe, a repair agent guided by Jev's diagnoses, which raises the security pass rate from 63.5% to 70.7%, above 66.1% for LLM-guided repair.

entry.title: DGF-Bench: A Benchmark for Simulating and Auditing Deception Against Multi-Agent Governance Boards
entry.summary: DGF-Bench: A Benchmark for Simulating and Auditing Deception Against Multi-Agent Governance Boards arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This arXiv paper introduces DGF-Bench, a benchmark in which AI agents act as a governance board reviewing synthetic project dossiers while an attacker plants deceptive content in unvouched evidence. Most tested models reached correct outcomes on nearly all gates without attacks, but attacks that imitate the organization's own process markedly lowered some models' correct-decision counts. The paper defines a DGF score for the share of attacks a model blocks and releases the open-source package dgf-bench to compute it.

entry.title: JEV as a Judge for Agent Trace Security: Comparing a Typed Model with Generative LLM Judges
entry.summary: JEV as a Judge for Agent Trace Security: An Empirical Comparison with Generative LLM Judges arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper examines whether JEV, a typed decision model, can serve as a judge for classifying security risks in tool-using agent traces, compared with generative LLM judges. Across four benchmarks totaling 5,219 trajectories, JEV achieves a higher average positive-class F1 (77.8) than the strongest generative configuration, GLM-5.2 (74.1). JEV's median latency is 0.99 seconds and its estimated cost is about $0.000195 per valid judgment. The authors conclude JEV is an economical screening signal, with trade-offs in precision and recall.

entry.title: Physics-Verified Federated Learning: Protecting Collaborative Anomaly Detection in Critical Water Infrastructure
entry.summary: Physics-Attested Federated Learning: Securing Collaborative Anomaly Detection in Critical Water Infrastructure arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper addresses data poisoning in federated learning, where fabricated telemetry can corrupt shared intrusion detection models. The authors use physical process invariants, such as conservation laws and actuator couplings, mined from clean data as a verifiable admission gate for federated updates. They evaluate seven aggregation rules on the SWaT and WADI water testbeds and the BATADAL benchmark against fabrication, replay poisoning, and adaptive adversaries. The paper also uses zk-SNARKs so clients can prove invariant compliance without revealing operational telemetry.

entry.title: Improving and securing image watermarking channels for traceable AI content.
entry.summary: Optimizing and Securing the Modern Watermarking Channel for Images arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Recent rules require traceable generated content, so modern watermarking uses post-hoc multi-bit schemes built from neural encoder-decoder pairs. The paper analyzes these networks statistically and shows they implicitly form parallel AWGN channels with BPSK modulation, which limits capacity and lacks a secret key, making them insecure. Based on this analysis, it introduces SNW, a post-hoc watermarking system that significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in capacity and offers strong security guarantees. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model deep watermarking encoder-decoder pairs as parallel BPSK-AWGN channels, link security to key estimability, and report that their SNW system exceeds baselines in capacity and approach

entry.title: StallGrid: A protocol-native tarpit that stalls scanners in industrial control systems, with internet-exposure measurements
entry.summary: StallGrid: Measuring Internet-exposed Engagement in Protocol-Native OT Tarpits arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents StallGrid, described as the first application-layer tarpit for OT/ICS, which stalls scanners using Modbus exception codes and prolonged IEC-104 connected states. Five variants ran for 24 days, logging 6,709 sessions and over 2,000 hours of accumulated connection engagement. The authors position protocol-native tarpitting as a low-cost complementary defense where patching is infeasible.

entry.title: AuxMark: A Watermark Against Unauthorized Agent Distillation
entry.summary: AuxMark: Defending Against Unauthorized Agent Distillation via Auxiliary Behavioral Watermarking arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces AuxMark, a behavioral watermarking framework for detecting when AI agent trajectories are illegally used to train student agents. It inserts harmless auxiliary actions into teacher agent trajectories and stores the surrounding context as private evidence cards, then audits suspect models through a black-box sign test. Across three agent benchmarks, two teacher agents, and four student architectures, the authors report detecting all 24 distilled models with zero false positives on 48 clean models. The method is also reported to remain effective against flooding, paraphrasing, truncation, and adaptive cleaning attacks.

entry.title: SEAD: A State-Based View of Attacks and Defenses in Tool-Using Agents
entry.summary: SEAD: A State-Based Perspective on Attack and Defense in Tool-Using Agents arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper frames attacks and defenses on language-model agents that use tools as partially observed state control, since earlier actions can change state so that a later routine-looking action becomes harmful. The attack method DART breaks harmful goals into locally plausible steps and uses real tool-execution feedback to guide search. The defense method SAGE investigates relevant state through read-only queries before allowing or blocking each action. Reported results include DART improving semantic attack success by 18.8 to 35.9 points, SAGE preserving 95.79% of benign trajectories while intercepting 92.73% of harmful paths, and reducing DART's executable attack success from 48.0% to 4.0% in online evaluation. ★★★★ Notable: Unifies attack and defense as partially observed state control, proposing DART for decomposed attacks and SAGE for pre-execution read-only defense; the authors report executable attack success falling

entry.title: CoDeL: Co-evolving defense that trains LLM agents to resist hidden prompt-injection attacks
entry.summary: CoDeL: Co-Evolutionary Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM-based Agents arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents CoDeL, a training-based defense that protects LLM-based agents from indirect prompt injection, where malicious instructions hide in external tools or content. The defender is updated with LoRA-based GDPO using a decoupled reward covering safety, task progress, and format compliance. A co-evolving prober searches for injections that still succeed against the current defender, creating a shifting training curriculum. Experiments on three benchmarks, nine baselines, and two base models report an 88.5% reduction in attack success rate. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes CoDeL, co-evolving a defender and prober that mines latency-guided injections into a moving curriculum; the authors report an 88.5% ASR reduction across three IPI benchmarks and nine baseline

entry.title: Evaluating How Well Windows Malware Detectors Resist Evasion Attacks
entry.summary: Breaking Windows Malware Detection: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Problem-Space Adversarial Robustness arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper evaluates nine state-of-the-art evasion attacks against eight Windows malware detectors, seven open-source and one commercial, while keeping modified samples executable. It measures robustness through attack effectiveness, complementarity, transferability, and adversarial hardening. The authors find that detector vulnerability depends on model representation and attack type, and that no detector family is uniformly robust across all attacks.

entry.title: ReproBench: Testing AI Agents on Rebuilding Software Vulnerabilities from Scratch
entry.summary: ReproBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Reproducing Vulnerability From Scratch arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces ReproBench, a benchmark that tests whether LLM agents can reproduce a vulnerability starting only from a CVE identifier, including rebuilding the execution environment. The reproduction workflow is split into six phases, each evaluated with verifiable artifacts. Using 30 real-world IoT firmware vulnerabilities, the authors found that 45.3% of runs resorted to vulnerability simulation, while only 5.3% of CVE-model pairs reproduced real vulnerabilities successfully.

entry.title: Quantum security of the XOR of random permutations, analyzed with Fourier methods
entry.summary: Quantum Security of XOR of Permutations via Fourier Analysis arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies whether the XOR of several independent random permutations (XoP) stays secure against quantum attacks that query it in superposition. The authors prove explicit upper bounds on the advantage of any q-query quantum algorithm in distinguishing XoP from a random function. The bounds hold across the whole query range well beyond the 2^(n/3) limit from quantum collision finding. The proof uses a Fourier-analytic version of the polynomial method. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show XOR of r≥2 random permutations is hard to distinguish from a random function under q quantum queries, via a Fourier-analytic polynomial method, claiming the first quantum beyond-birth

entry.title: Before Agents Act: Assurance-Aware Semantic Scheduling for Distributed Evidence Acquisition
entry.summary: Before Agents Act: Assurance-Aware Semantic Scheduling for Evidence Acquisition in Distributed Systems arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper proposes Assurance-Aware Semantic Scheduling (AAS), which jointly selects witnesses and schedules evidence acquisition under quorum, diversity, freshness, deadline, and resource constraints, so that tool-using agents do not act on expired evidence before infrastructure changes. In three generated infrastructure workloads, AAS produced 1,075 of 1,200 valid candidates versus 647 for a constraint-aware forward scheduler, and reduced stale candidates from 440 to 12. The authors stress these are controlled simulation results, that the bounded oracle shares a temporal search component, and that transfer to deployed systems is untested.

entry.title: RADNPO: A reference-free method for making LLMs forget specific content
entry.summary: RADNPO: Reference-free Adaptive Negative Preference Optimization for LLM Unlearning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Large language models can memorize sensitive, private, or copyrighted text from pre-training, so unlearning methods are needed to remove targeted knowledge. This paper proposes RADNPO, which suppresses forget targets while explicitly guiding how the next-token probability is redistributed. It contrasts each target with alternative tokens favored by the current distribution and adjusts forgetting strength using target confidence and distribution concentration. Experiments on TOFU and MUSE show it achieves a better trade-off between forgetting quality and model utility than current baselines.

entry.title: Long-term outage planning using scenario-based system load forecasts
entry.summary: Long-Term Operational Planning Using Scenario-Based System Load Forecasting arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Rapid growth of hyperscale data centers in Northern Virginia is increasing electricity demand, requiring transmission reinforcement that needs planned outages evaluated months ahead. Conventional studies use monthly or seasonal peak-load assumptions, which can be overly conservative and cause short outages to be postponed or denied. This paper compares daily, weekly, and monthly load forecasts built with SARIMA, Prophet, Gradient Boosting, and Random Forest, reconciled bottom-up across horizons, against peak-based methods. Results indicate granular forecasts reduce unnecessary conservatism and accommodate outages better, especially short ones, without changing reliability criteria.

entry.title: Faultless: a technique for checking whether neural decompilers' code matches the original program.
entry.summary: Faultless: A Program Equivalence Technique for Validating and Evaluating Neural Decompilers arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces Faultless, a program equivalence technique for translation validation of neural decompilers. It compares neural decompiler output with code from a deterministic decompiler or a reference solution. The authors note that neural decompilation poses challenges such as limited extrafunctional context and systematic semantic inconsistencies, which existing methods do not handle well. Faultless uses a static symbolic execution approach with an execution model and memory model designed for these challenges.

entry.title: LoRo-Mark: A Provably Lossless and Robust Watermark for LLM Agents
entry.summary: LoRo-Mark:Provably Lossless and Robust Agent Watermarking arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper addresses the problem of LLM agents being repackaged and presented under another party's identity. It proposes LoRo-Mark, a watermarking mechanism that embeds ownership evidence without affecting normal functionality. The watermark is placed in a cryptographically authenticated forensic branch that activates only on owner-authorized requests, and ownership information is redundantly spread across forensic behavior sequences for recovery after partial modification. Experiments on multiple LLM agents report no degradation on normal tasks and reliable ownership verification under sequence modifications.

entry.title: GateDrain: Availability attacks and admission defense for confidence-gated edge-cloud AI
entry.summary: GateDrain: Availability Attacks and Admission-Side Defense for Confidence-Gated Edge-Cloud Inference arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper shows that confidence-gated edge-cloud inference, which sends uncertain inputs to a cloud model, creates an availability attack surface. The proposed GateDrain attack uses bounded input perturbations to lower confidence, redirecting requests that would be answered locally into a shared cloud queue without raising the application request rate. The authors also propose Bounded Escalation, a containment defense combining per-source admission budgets, protected capacity, and trusted-class priority. The paper notes that tighter aggregate containment can reject legitimate unauthenticated offloads and reduce overall accuracy through edge fallback.

entry.title: Privacy risks of crowdsourced fine-tuning: poisoning data to extract others' records
entry.summary: The Privacy Fallacy of Crowdsourced Fine-Tuning: Extracting Proprietary Data via Topic-Based Poisoning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper examines a privacy risk in supervised fine-tuning of language models that uses crowdsourced user conversations, where untrusted users can contribute data. The authors show that a malicious user can poison a small fraction of the data to amplify extraction of other users' unseen instructions, using only black-box, output-only access to the model. Experiments on four models and two datasets show near-verbatim extraction rising to 3.71 times the unpoisoned rate with 50 poisoned examples. The authors also find that data filtering detects poisoned samples poorly, with the best method reaching only 0.378 F-1.

entry.title: TrackFlood: Shifting Latency Attacks from NMS-Free Detectors to Real-Time Trackers
entry.summary: TrackFlood: Relocating Latency Attacks from NMS-Free Detectors to Real-Time Trackers arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies latency attacks on object detectors, aiming to make systems respond too late rather than corrupt predictions, with real-time applications such as autonomous driving in mind. The authors propose TrackFlood, a white-box overload attack that floods the tracker in NMS-free detect-then-track pipelines with phantom detections while detector inference stays unchanged. Tests on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin show tracker latency rising substantially, and a lightweight bounded-admission layer is evaluated as a mitigation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors argue NMS-free detectors remain latency-attackable, relocating the surface to downstream tracking; on Jetson, TrackFlood raises tracker latency while detector latency stays flat, with mode

entry.title: A2A-ForensicTrace: offline checking of tamper-evident records from agent-to-agent interactions
entry.summary: A2A-ForensicTrace: Offline Verification of Tamper-Evident A2A Runtime Evidence arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents A2A-ForensicTrace, an offline verification layer for runtime evidence from Agent2Agent (A2A) executions. It turns runtime observations into typed records, derives protocol-related relationships, and commits them under an incident-trace root, with an Ed25519-signed receipt binding the root to the incident context. The evaluation ran 240 executions through the official A2A SDK, including 120 condition runs and 120 matched controls, and all condition runs returned the expected findings while no control raised an indication.

entry.title: Training Witnesses: Verifying training runs without trusting the trainer
entry.summary: Training Witnesses: Trusting the Training without Trusting the Trainer arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces Witnesses, a method for certifying neural network training, data usage, and evaluation. It relies on fast behavioral fingerprints combined with occasional replay challenges to audit training, with low overhead for the trainer and low cost for the verifier. The method was tested on language model training runs from 100M to 2B parameters, and the authors also propose a self-regulating leaderboard of auto-certified runs to support shared baselines and reproducibility. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes auditing training with behavioral fingerprints and occasional replay challenges, shifting the verification burden to the trainer; the authors report low overhead on 100M–2B language models un

entry.title: A2A-CaseVerify: Merkle-linked verification of case evidence for cross-organization A2A workflows
entry.summary: A2A-CaseVerify: Merkle-Linked Case-Evidence Verification for Cross-Organization A2A Workflows arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper presents A2A-CaseVerify, a deterministic offline verifier that maps A2A runtime objects, business events and typed support edges into a directed case evidence graph committed by a deterministic Merkle root. It returns SUPPORTED only when protection and profile-specific reconstruction checks pass. Evaluated on one canonical healthcare-profile bundle and 13 controlled mutations, the canonical and SDK-generated bundles were accepted and all mutations were rejected.

entry.title: Near-duplicate families cause false membership attribution for exact records
entry.summary: Near-Duplicate Families Break Exact-Record Membership Inference arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Membership inference asks whether a specific record was in a model's training set and is increasingly used as evidence in data provenance and copyright auditing. The paper shows that near-duplicate content common in web-scale data confounds standard methods: on CC-News, a clean-reference LiRA auditor labeled 99.70% of family-present exact non-members as members at a 1.00% false-positive rate. The authors conclude that positive model-only evidence may establish family-level exposure without establishing exact-record provenance. ★★★★★ Notable: Introduces a four-world audit showing near-duplicate families cause severe false membership attribution; the authors report that a clean-reference LiRA auditor labels 99.70% of family-present exact no

entry.title: Can prompt anonymity stop LLM providers from re-identifying users?
entry.summary: Can Prompt Anonymity Protect Your Identity From LLM Providers? arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper examines whether anonymizing proxies, which separate user identity from prompts, still let LLM providers re-identify users through the prompt content they can see. The authors built PromptAnonBench, a benchmark of over 175,000 cleaned multi-turn prompts from SWE-Chat and WildChat. Even with text-based defenses, an attacker could re-identify at least one anonymized conversation for 50–75% of SWE-Chat users and up to 10% of WildChat users at a 10% false acceptance rate.

entry.title: "No Free Efficiency": a paper on how making model training cheaper can weaken robustness and security.
entry.summary: No Free Efficiency: Revisiting the Trade-off Between Training Efficiency and Model Vulnerability arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper systematically studies the trade-off between training efficiency and model vulnerability across vision and language models. It finds that efficiency-oriented training increases susceptibility to adversarial and privacy attacks, linked to sharper loss geometry and changed representational structure. Models trained with simplified zero RL recipes show greater catastrophic forgetting and overconfidence than those trained with conventional alignment. The authors call for multi-objective training that jointly optimizes performance, cost, and security.

entry.title: The Cost of Stability: Deanonymizing Onion Services' Long-Lived Introduction Circuits
entry.summary: The Cost of Stability: Deanonymizing Onion Services Long-Lived Introduction Circuits arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents an intersection attack that exploits the fixed 18 to 24 hour introduction circuits used by Tor onion services. An adversary observing one Tor relay at a time can use this stability to identify an onion service's network location. The authors tested the attack on the live Tor network against a self-operated service, reconstructing the full circuit in all nine end-to-end runs. They also propose periodically rebuilding internal introduction circuits to limit evidence accumulation without changing publicly advertised information. ★★★★★ Notable: Exploits the design in which onion service introduction circuits stay fixed for 18 to 24 hours to propose an intersection attack that lets an adversary observing one relay at a time locate an onion se

entry.title: RAISE: Improving LLM Access-Control Policy Synthesis with Symbolic Evaluation
entry.summary: RAISE: Reinforcing Access Control Policy Synthesis in LLMs via Symbolic Evaluation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper introduces CedarInstruct, a dataset of 5,800 scenarios across 44 domains with verified target policies and executable verification plans for Cedar policy synthesis. It proposes RAISE, a two-stage method combining verified supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning driven by verifier signals. The RAISE-OC variant, which uses failed checks and symbolic counterexamples for guided exploration, is reported to outperform zero-shot GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 on held-out semantic success, and the training transfers to the independently built CedarBench.

entry.title: Tokens Change, Structure Endures: Spectral Watermarking for Generated Speech
entry.summary: Tokens Change, Structure Endures: Spectral Watermarking for Generated Speech arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper proposes Redwing, a training-free token-level watermarking method for AI-generated speech that works during generation. It addresses retokenization, where decoding speech to audio and re-encoding it changes token identities and weakens the watermark. Redwing builds a graph from observed token substitutions and jointly optimizes embedding and detection functions over its Laplacian basis. On the Moshi system after eight Mimi resynthesis passes, it reaches 80.7% TPR at 1% FPR, versus 8.3% for KGW. ★★★★ Notable: Redwing builds a graph Laplacian basis from retokenization substitutions and jointly optimizes embedding and detection; on Moshi after eight Mimi passes it reports 80.7% TPR versus 8.3% for KGW and at

entry.title: SecProbe: An adaptive test of whether coding AI agents can spot and fix security flaws
entry.summary: SecProbe: Adaptive Evaluation of Coding Agents on Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 SecProbe is a framework that adaptively evaluates coding agents on cybersecurity vulnerabilities by combining Item Response Theory with on-demand synthesis of repository-scale vulnerability-repair tasks. The authors built 353 tasks covering six programming languages and 151 CWE types, and evaluated nine frontier models with two agent harnesses. Success rates peaked at 28.33%, and compared with random and one-shot baselines, SecProbe gave comparable ability estimates while requiring up to 29.5% fewer tasks.

entry.title: MAD-Guard: Comparing Token Generation and Direct Decision Outputs for Multimodal Forensic Tasks
entry.summary: MAD-Guard: Controlled Study of Autoregressive Generation versus Direct Decision Interfaces for Closed Multimodal Forensic Tasks arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies whether multimodal models need to generate tokens autoregressively or can output forensic decisions directly. Using the same backbone and training budget, it compares several decision interfaces on latency, calibration error, and accuracy. A binary direct head cuts latency by 2.60 to 7.27 times and lowers calibration error, at a small accuracy cost, while multi-task and contrastive head variants outperform the autoregressive baseline. Across five benchmarks, the approach performs well on synthetic, camouflage, and document forgeries but shows a clear limitation on compressed face manipulation.

entry.title: COGNIT-Guard: A calibrated safety filter that screens prompts on a CPU and NPU before they reach a language model
entry.summary: COGNIT-Guard: Calibrated Standalone Direct-Decision Guardrails with Heterogeneous CPU-NPU Confidence Cascading under Explicit Latency and False-Positive Constraints arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents COGNIT-Guard, a real-time system that checks user prompts for safety before they reach a target LLM. A fast CPU gatekeeper hands uncertain cases to a 322M-parameter direct-decision model running on an NPU. On the unseen DUCS-Bench test split it reports 98.85% accuracy and a 0.42% benign false-positive rate, with mean latency of 41.63 ms for the cascade. The authors also evaluate out-of-domain accuracy on SafetyBench-ZH and show that experience replay recovers performance lost to alignment.

entry.title: The Cost of Peeking: Anytime-Valid Leakage Detection on ML-KEM Traces
entry.summary: The Price of Peeking: Anytime-Valid Leakage Detection on ML-KEM EM Traces arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 Side-channel evaluators often check leakage tests during data collection and decide whether to continue or stop based on the results. This paper studies anytime-valid leakage detection using betting-based tests, which keep the false-alarm probability controlled at all times under an explicit conditional symmetry null. On an open ML-KEM electromagnetic dataset, the method needed about 1.68 to 2.38 times as many traces as a fixed-horizon randomization test to detect leakage in synthetic and degraded recordings. On undegraded recordings, the monitored procedure stopped early, with median stopping points of 62 to 316 traces.

entry.title: Information Blackhole: a study of backdoor attacks on 3D point cloud autoencoders
entry.summary: Information Blackhole: Exploring Backdoor Mechanism in 3D Point Cloud Reconstruction arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 Point cloud autoencoders are core tools for representing 3D scenes, yet backdoor attacks on them remain little studied. The paper argues that the generative latent space mixes benign and malicious data, so reconstructions can collapse toward the source data. The authors propose the Information Blackhole principle and Adaptive Gaussian Matching (AGM), which regularizes poisoned latent distributions to improve attack controllability. Experiments on ModelNet and ShapeNetPart are reported.

entry.title: Where the Numbers Come From: Auditing Provenance-Based Intrusion Detection Evaluation
entry.summary: Where the Numbers Come From: Auditing Evaluation in Provenance-Based Intrusion Detection arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 The paper audits nine released provenance-based intrusion detector implementations and runs four of them with their own code. It identifies three measurement effects: ThreaTrace reports 0.938 precision with neighbourhood credit, though only 7 of its 994 alarms carry its own attack label; removing test-label checkpoint selection lowers attack detection precision by 0.16 to 0.33; and a buffer-reuse defect gives a linear encoder unintended degree-dependent inputs.

entry.title: What It Means to Forget a Person: Individual-Level Unlearning in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: What Does It Mean to Forget a Person? Individual-Level Unlearning in Vision-Language Models arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper introduces IDUnlearn-Bench, the first benchmark for individual-level multimodal unlearning in vision-language models (VLMs). It represents each person as connected multimodal evidence and evaluates four task families: attribute access, identity access, identity binding, and identity reconstruction. Experiments show that attribute-centric forgetting often leaves substantial identity-level knowledge intact, and that reducing one risk can amplify another.

entry.title: HESP: A controller that separates what to probe from when to stop in local LLM alert triage
entry.summary: HESP: Separating What to Probe from When to Stop in Local LLM Alert-Triage Agents arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 Security operations centers receive more alerts than analysts can handle, and organizations that cannot send telemetry to hosted models must automate triage with small open-weight LLMs on their own hardware. The paper presents HESP, a controller that keeps the investigation procedure outside the model, tracking competing explanations, choosing read-only probes by expected information gain per cost, accepting only evidence-backed verdicts, and ending investigations itself. Across five open-weight models (7B to 72B) and 7,272 audited episodes in a controlled triage environment, HESP substantially raises verified completion, showing that choosing what to probe and deciding when to stop are separable failures.

entry.title: Bypassing Expression Sandboxes in Orchestration Platforms: Flaws in Enumerate-and-Block Security
entry.summary: Weird Machine Compositors: Exploiting AI Orchestration at the Expression Layer arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper argues that enumerate-and-block expression sandboxes in orchestration platforms are fundamentally unfixable. Using n8n's expression sandbox, the authors demonstrate three escalating bypasses that produced three CVEs. They also describe a trust laundering pattern and how AI-assisted enumeration speeds up discovery of coverage gaps, and they offer a coverage analysis method, an open-source tool, and an allowlist-based mitigation.

entry.title: Why API secrets should stay out of LLM tokens: threat analysis and vault-mediated execution for AI agents
entry.summary: API Secrets Should Never Become Tokens in the LLM's Vocabulary: A Threat Analysis of API Credential Handling in LLM Agent Systems and an Empirical Evaluation of a Vault-Mediated Execution Boundary arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper examines how API credentials can leak when tool-using LLM agents handle them, such as through prompts, logs, or memory. It proposes a vault-mediated design in which the model picks a connector identifier while a trusted boundary supplies authentication. In two controlled black-box experiments on the Corvic Security Vault implementation, all 16 probes met their expected outcomes, with the credential absent from the locations tested. The authors also report a failed connector configuration and state that vault mediation is necessary but not sufficient.

entry.title: Security Analysis of 84 Candidate Public-Key Schemes in a Chinese Crypto Competition
entry.summary: Cryptanalysis of the ICCS NGCC Round-1 Public-Key Candidates IACR ePrint · Sep 27, 2026 This paper reviews the 84 public-key candidates submitted to the ICCS NGCC round-1 public evaluation, focusing on design flaws that local code fixes cannot resolve. It identifies eight such weaknesses, similar to known pitfalls from NIST post-quantum standardization, including sub-ring projections that reduce IND-CPA security, public data that exposes supposedly secret values, static key reuse without a chosen-ciphertext transform, and rejection sampling that leaks an equivalent signing key. The authors state that all findings were obtained with AI assistance and provide a link to their artifacts.

entry.title: Closing the Gap: Rigorously Proving and Strengthening RPKI Security
entry.summary: Mind the Gap: Proving and Improving RPKI IACR ePrint · Sep 27, 2026 This paper presents the first rigorous security analysis of the Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI), an IETF standard that protects inter-domain routing against prefix and subprefix hijacks. Using modular security specifications, it analyzes RPKI's interactions with BGP and IP and identifies sufficient conditions under which RPKI provably meets its goals. The authors find that existing deployments do not always satisfy these conditions, for example due to circular dependencies, and propose standard-compliant improvements.

entry.title: Enhanced parallel attacks on EC-HMQV-C and ECMQV protocols
entry.summary: Enhanced Embarrassingly Parallel Attacks against EC-HMQV-C and ECMQV IACR ePrint · Sep 27, 2026 This paper extends a 2025 parallel impersonation attack by Sarr on ECMQV and EC-HMQV-C to a multi-party setting with initiators and responders. It presents three attacks with estimated parallel running times and per-processor memory costs. For a 128-bit EC-HMQV-C instance on an idealized massively parallel architecture, the improved attack is said to correspond to 78 bits of security in parallel time.

entry.title: Practical null-branch witness attacks on AIMer v2.0 in-the-head signatures
entry.summary: Practical Null-Branch Witness Attacks on In-the-Head Signatures IACR ePrint · Sep 27, 2026 This paper presents a classical, public-key-only forgery attack on the AIM2-based AIMer v2.0 signature scheme, which was selected in Korea's KpqC competition. For every honestly generated public key, the authors claim signatures on arbitrary messages can be forged without signing queries. The attack exploits zero factors that leave intermediate values unconstrained, completing them into witnesses that satisfy the full relation. The paper also argues that a satisfying witness need not decode to a one-way function preimage, revealing a gap in AIMer's security reduction.

entry.title: Complete classification of whole-output linear structures in FEILIAN-type components
